skill1: Police Badge: Creates a Shield equal to 100% of the skill user's final Max HP for 10 sec. — the named STATUS 'Police Badge' itself (a self-status gating the burst branch) is not modeled; only the shield event is emitted. No HP pool exists at scope lock, so the shield absorbs nothing.
skill2: Equally shares damage taken for 10 sec.

Continuously recovers 5% of the skill user's final Max HP every 1 sec for 5 sec. — the HP amount is unmodeled (no HP pool); only the 5 recovery EVENTS are emitted, to feed teammates' on-recovery triggers.
burst: Gains Indomitability for 5 sec. Removes Police Badge.

Creates a shared Shield equal to 40% of the skill user's final Max HP that protects all allies from damage. Lasts for 10 sec. — 'shared/protects all allies' scoping is not modeled; the shield event is emitted to self only (see caveats).

caveats: ⚑ skill1 block 1 trigger: 'Activates after 5 normal attack(s)' is modeled as hitCount:5. Poli is an SG with hitsPerShot 10 — if the game counts a normal ATTACK as one trigger pull (not one pellet/hit), the true threshold is 5 TRIGGER PULLS = 50 engine hits. hitCount counts ROUNDS per the schema comment, and an SG round is one trigger pull, so count:5 is the literal read; but the pellet/round ambiguity is the single largest uncertainty in this override (a 10x cadence error on a team-wide ATK buff).
⚑ skill2 block 1 trigger: 'every 20 sec' with no activation clause → interval:20, first fire at t=20s. Whether the game fires this at t=0 or t=20 is kit-silent.

⚑ skill2 block 2 trigger: 'Activates when Police Badge ends' — the Badge is created at battle start for 10 sec, so it ends at t≈10s (or earlier, when the burst removes it). Modeled as a ONE-SHOT-shaped interval:10 approximation; the engine has no badge-status clock, so this RE-FIRES every 10s, over-emitting recovery events. See flags — a real fix needs either a one-shot trigger primitive or a targetStatus-style self-status clock.

⚑ burst shield target: the kit says the 40% shield 'protects all allies', but the shield effect's maxHpPct is caster-scaled and the engine emits per-target 'shielded' events. Modeled as self-only to avoid over-firing teammates' shielded-triggers off ONE shared shield instance; if the game applies a distinct shield instance per ally, target should be {kind:'allies'}. Damage-inert either way EXCEPT for a teammate with a 'shielded' trigger.

poli is offensively near-inert at scope lock beyond her two ATK buffs: DEF is inert in v1, shields/heals model no HP, and Indomitability/damage-sharing are pure survivability. Her whole simulated contribution is the 5.46% rolling team ATK buff, the 44.55% burst ATK buff, and burst-gauge generation.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Poli (SG/Water/Defender/Burst II). Full-kit audit: 8 kit lines, 6 IMPLEMENTED, 2 SKIPPED (damage-sharing, Indomitability — both pure defensive with no v1 surface). Load-bearing ⚑: (1) the S1 hitCount:5 threshold — SG pellet-vs-round ambiguity is a potential 10x cadence error on a team-wide ATK buff, the single value most worth measuring; (2) the S2b 'when Police Badge ends' trigger, approximated as interval:10 because the engine has no self-status clock, which re-fires every 10s instead of once. Heals/shields are kept (never skipped on isolation) so a teammate's on-recovery / on-shielded triggers fire; the HP magnitudes are recorded for completeness and are inert at scope lock. DEF ▲23.51% is kept as defPct (engine-inert in v1) for kit completeness. Burst ATK ▲44.55% is keyed burstCast (poli's OWN burst block, self-mode-shaped) — it lands pre-FB and is FB-major-exempt by cast timing, which is correct for a burst-cast stat buff. No noFb set anywhere (no function-damage riders in this kit); no damage lines at all — poli contributes ZERO direct skill damage.

flags.estimate: 5 (literal kit read: 5 normal attacks = 5 trigger pulls)
flags.reasoning: Poli is a Shotgun with hitsPerShot 10. The engine's hitCount trigger 'counts ROUNDS not pulls' per the schema, and for an SG one trigger pull is one round that sprays 10 pellets — so 5 rounds is the literal reading. BUT if the engine's hit accumulator increments per PELLET/hit rather than per round, count:5 fires after half a trigger pull — a ~10x over-cadence on a team-wide ATK buff. This is the single highest-leverage uncertainty in the override: at 5 rounds with 9 ammo the buff refreshes ~twice per magazine and is effectively permanent uptime; at 50 hits it also lands near-permanently, so the DAMAGE difference may be small — but the buffApply cadence differs by 10x and any downstream stack/consumer would diverge.
flags.recipe: Instrument: run controlComp('poli') with cfg.onEvent, filter buffApply where stat==='atkPct' && value===5.46, and count applications per magazine against the shot events. Cross-check the engine's hitCount accumulator in src/engine/sim.ts (does it add 1 per shot or hitsPerShot per shot for an SG?). If per-pellet, set count:50. This is answerable from CODE alone — no footage needed — and should be resolved before any board A/B.

flags.estimate: interval sec:10 (Badge starts t=0, lasts 10s → ends t=10s)
flags.reasoning: The kit trigger is a one-shot status-expiry event. The engine has no self-status expiry trigger and no primitive for 'fire once at t=N'. interval:10 first-fires at t=10 (correct) but then RE-FIRES at 20/30/…/180 — over-emitting 5 recovery events every 10 sec for the whole fight, i.e. ~90 spurious recovery events. That is damage-inert alone but WILL over-feed a teammate with a 'recovery' trigger (crown-style on-recovery buffs), which is a real over-credit in a comp containing one. Also, the burst REMOVES the Badge early, which would move the real expiry earlier on the first rotation — unmodeled.
flags.recipe: Two options, both cheap: (a) if a one-shot primitive is wanted, the closest existing shape is a `targetStatus`-style clock, but that channel is enemy-only — so this needs an engine primitive (out of scope for a parser baseline); (b) pragmatically, if the comp contains no 'recovery'-trigger ally, drop this block entirely (fully inert) and record it in unmodeled. Decide by grepping the graded comps for a `recovery` trigger; if none, the choice is provably damage-zero and the simplest correct move is to keep it as authored and note the limitation.

flags.reasoning: 'Creates a shared Shield … that protects all allies' is ONE shield instance covering the team, not five instances. Targeting {kind:'allies'} would emit 5 separate 'shielded' events, over-firing any teammate's shielded-gated block (naga-style requiresShielded / shielded triggers) five times over for a single game-side shield. Targeting self emits one event and under-covers teammates. Neither is exactly right; self is the under-crediting choice, which is the correct default under measured>fudge.
flags.recipe: Only matters in a comp with a `shielded`-trigger or `requiresShielded`-gated ally. Grep overrides for trigger kind 'shielded' / block gate requiresShielded; if a co-teammate carries one, record a real fight with that pairing and read whether the teammate's shield-gated effect goes live for ALL allies or only poli. Until then keep self.

flags.estimate: first fire at t=20s (schema default for interval)
flags.reasoning: 'every 20 sec' carries no activation clause, so it is an interval trigger. The schema states interval first-fires at t=sec. Whether the game fires it at battle start (t=0) or after the first 20s window is kit-silent; a t=0 first fire would shift every subsequent activation 20s earlier.
flags.recipe: Damage-inert here (defPct is engine-inert in v1), so this needs no measurement unless a future consumer reads DEF. If ever needed: read the DEF-buff icon appearance frame off a recording anchored to the 03:00→02:59 frame.
